To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the treatment of liver metastases from neuroendocrine tumors is still challenging and that the role of systemic chemotherapy has not been clearly defined.

1) in patients with advanced carcinoid syndrome, octreotide-LAR is superior to placebo in terms of progression-free survival; 2) in patients with carcinoids and liver metastases, the efficacy of octreotide-Lar is superior to that of interferon-alpha; 3) in patients with pancreatic NET, sunitinb and everolimus improve progression-free survival.

(1) surgical resection or hepatic artery chemoembolization may be considered as therapeutic options in patients whose disease is limited to the liver; (2) patients with “carcinoids” and “functional” pancreatic NET may benefit from treatment with octreotide L.A.R.; (3) patients with advanced NET should be treated with sunitinib and everolimus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new treatment for neuroendocrine tumors.
the development of new therapies for the treatment of patients with liver metastases of neuroendocrine tumors.
the development of new therapies and treatment strategies for patients with liver metastases in patients with NET of gastroesophagealistric and pancreatic origin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single treatment for liver metastases from GEP-NETs and that the best treatment for an individual patient is determined by the patient’s performance status and the extent of disease.
patients with GEP-NETs should be evaluated by multidisciplinary teams to identify the best treatment options.

there is a need for a multidisciplinary approach to the treatment of liver metastases in patients with GEP-NETs, and the choice of therapy should be individualized according to tumor characteristics, clinical presentation, and patient performance status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment of liver metastases in patients with NET of GEP origin is based on the type and extent of disease, and the presence of carcinoid or functional PNET syndrome.
the treatment of liver metastases in patients with NET is a rapidly evolving field.

we have demonstrated the efficacy of somatostatin receptor scintigraphy in the diagnosis of liver metastases in patients with gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, and we have also demonstrated that the treatment of patients with liver-dominant metastases from gastroenteropancretatic neuroendocrine neoplasms is associated with improved survival, particularly in patients with carcinoids and well differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

patients with liver metastasis from GEP-NETs should be treated by multidisciplinary team, including medical oncologist, gastroenterologist, endocrinologist, surgeon, interventional radiologist, pathologist, and nuclear medicine specialist.
there is a need to better define the role of systemic therapies in patients with carcinoids and pancreatic NET liver-only metastasis.
there are several treatment options available for patients with NETs with liver metastasis.
